commodity: Passenger vehicles — BMW X3 (20d and 30e plug-in hybrid) for global export
operations: BMW Group Plant Rosslyn, 9 Frans du Toit Street, Rosslyn (Tshwane); wholly owned by BMW AG (Munich); head office Midrand
scale_note: Plant Rosslyn produced 79,000+ vehicles in 2025 on three shifts; ~2,800 associates at the plant; R4.2bn (EUR200m+) electrification investment for 4th-gen X3 PHEV (SOP late 2024); 100,000th 4th-gen X3 built by early 2026. Electricity: PPA with Bio2Watt Bronkhorstspruit biogas plant (4.4 MW) since Oct 2015 supplying 25-30% of plant electricity; BMW Group Report 2023 says biogas plant expansion in 2024-25 will let the plant 'rely almost entirely on renewable energy'; on-site solar PV only 66 kWp (Building 84); zero waste to landfill since 2021. No SA-specific Scope 2 target published - group target is 100% green electricity at all plants.

commodity: Passenger, van and truck tyres (Continental, General Tire, Barum); OE supply to SA vehicle makers
operations: Single tyre plant in Gqeberha (Nelson Mandela Bay) - Continental's only tyre plant in Africa; 100% owned by Continental AG (Hanover) since 2013; sales/marketing and BestDrive retail network run from same site
scale_note: 1,100+ employees. Steam raising switched from coal to biomass + LPG (completed as part of Continental's global coal/HFO phase-out, all plants by Jan 2026). Continental group policy: all purchased electricity from renewable sources since 2020 (via certificates), 20% energy-consumption cut by 2030 vs 2018, climate-neutral production by 2040 - so a wheeled PPA would displace the certificate-based approach. No on-site solar size or unit capacity published on official pages.

commodity: Domestic appliances — stoves, ovens, hobs, tumble dryers, top-load washers (Jacobs); refrigerators and chest freezers incl. solar off-grid range (Ezakheni)
operations: Two plants: Jacobs, Durban (135 Teakwood Road, company-owned, head office) and Ezakheni, Ladysmith (leased); East London fridge plant no longer listed by company, dtic or Beko 2024 report - treat as closed/consolidated. 100% owned by Beko (formerly Arçelik, Istanbul) since 2011; also regional hub exporting to 35 sub-Saharan countries
scale_note: 2,000+ employees (dtic/SAnews 2023); 1.5-2 million appliances a year; R2.6bn invested over 15 years, further R500m pledged Jul 2025. Electricity: 1 MW rooftop solar at Jacobs supplies 13% of that factory's electricity (Aug 2025); solar for the leased Ezakheni site under discussion; energy-efficiency upgrades to high-temperature enamelling lines planned. Parent Beko target: 100% green electricity in manufacturing by 2030 (60.5% in 2024, 90.2 MWp own capacity) - SA plants must close the gap, likely via PPA.

commodity: Faurecia/Forvia: catalytic converters, exhaust systems, injected interior trims, seat and interior systems; Lear: seating and heating systems; Yazaki: wiring harnesses
operations: Forvia (Nanterre): Faurecia Clean Mobility plants at Retreat Cape Town (SA head office, 568 staff), Neave Township Gqeberha (320), Rosslyn Automotive Supplier Park (364) plus Faurecia Interior Systems at Kariega (NMB Logistics Park) and Rosslyn. Lear Corporation (Southfield, USA): Gqeberha (Neave Township, 1,500 staff), Rosslyn and East London. Yazaki: no standalone SA plant found - Yazaki's SA presence is Hesto Harnesses, its JV with Metair, in Stanger KZN (see p-hesto-harnesses-feltex-shatterprufe) - treat the Yazaki leg as a duplicate of that record.
scale_note: Combined SA headcount roughly 2,750 across the named Faurecia and Lear sites (NAACAM). No on-site solar, wheeled PPA or SA Scope 2 target published for any of the three; Forvia group target is CO2-neutral scopes 1+2 by 2025 (group-level, via green electricity purchases) which makes the SA plants natural PPA candidates. Individual sites are small (300-600 staff, tier-1 component plants) so load per site is modest.

commodity: Ford Ranger pickup (incl. Ranger PHEV from Mar 2025) for SA and 100+ export markets; diesel engines (Struandale)
operations: Silverton Manufacturing Plant, Pretoria (Ford Motor Company of Southern Africa (Manufacturing) (Pty) Ltd, wholly owned by Ford Motor Company, Dearborn) and Struandale Engine Plant, Gqeberha (R600m 2021 upgrade for V6 diesel). Head office moved to new Pretoria HQ 2026.
scale_note: Silverton capacity 200,000 vehicles/yr (720/day) after R15.8bn 2021 upgrade; ~4,535 employees at Silverton (Jun 2026), Ford SA total ~5,500 at peak. Electricity: 13.5 MWp SolarAfrica-built solar carport (30,226 panels) switched on May 2022 - supplied 35% of plant electricity at launch, Ford's 2025 article puts it at 18% of energy per Ranger after volume growth; 'Project Blue Oval' phase 2 (biogas/biomass co-generation) announced for 2024 but no completion reported, so a large gap remains. Ford global target: 100% carbon-free electricity in manufacturing by 2035, carbon neutral 2050. Struandale: no on-site generation published.

commodity: Hesto: automotive wiring harnesses and instrument clusters; Feltex: acoustic/soft trim, PU foam seats, carpets, heatshields, accessories; Shatterprufe: laminated windscreens and toughened auto glass
operations: Three unrelated owners bundled in one record. Hesto Harnesses (Metair 74.9% / Yazaki 25.1%; consolidated Metair subsidiary from 1 Apr 2025): 90,000 m2+ campus at Stanger/KwaDukuza, KZN, supplying Toyota, Isuzu, Ford Ranger. Feltex (KAP Ltd, Johannesburg): 19 plants incl. Jacobs HQ, Hammarsdale, Prospecton, Rosslyn, Silverton, Gqeberha, East London, plus JVs Feltex Fehrer, Autoneum Feltex, Auria SA. Shatterprufe (PG Group, Johannesburg): three auto-glass plants, HQ 1 Armourplate Road, Struandale, Gqeberha.
scale_note: Hesto ~5,000 staff per hesto.com (target 7,000), ~8,000 per Jun 2025 trade-press interview; revenue tripled to ~USD300m after Ford Ranger harness award; 4,000+ jobs added at the 2022 Stanger expansion (70% women). Shatterprufe 1,175 staff, 4m+ glass pieces/yr across three plants. Feltex headcount not published. No on-site solar, wheeled PPA or Scope 2 target published for any of the three; Metair 2025 restructuring and Ford 'rightsizing' make Hesto cost-sensitive for 2026.

commodity: Isuzu D-MAX bakkies and N/F-series trucks (assembly), incl. CNG truck (2024)
operations: Struandale assembly plant and head office, Gqeberha; Isuzu Motors South Africa (Pty) Ltd formed 2018 when Isuzu Motors Ltd (Tokyo) took over the former GM SA plant; adjacent R750m VSL Manufacturing D-MAX body-part plant opened late 2025
scale_note: 2025: ~26,000 vehicles retailed in SA (+12.2%) plus 5,371 exported to Africa (+4.5%); new D-MAX and next-gen trucks launching 2026. Plant capacity and headcount not published on official pages. Energy: IMSAf Environmental Roadmap targets 50% cut in Scope 1+2 CO2 by 2030 vs 2013 (54% already achieved), zero waste to landfill since 2016, and states renewable-energy implementation is planned for FY27 - no on-site solar or PPA reported yet, so this is a live procurement window.

commodity: Mercedes-Benz C-Class (6th generation, incl. plug-in hybrid) for export
operations: Mercedes-Benz South Africa Ltd Manufacturing, East London plant (IDZ-adjacent, own harbour access); wholly owned by Mercedes-Benz AG (Stuttgart), part of the C-Class global production network; head office Zwartkop, Centurion. Business Day (10 Mar 2026) reported GWM in talks to share the East London plant.
scale_note: ~2,400-3,300 employees (sources vary: MB careers page 3,300; 2025 press 2,400-2,500); ~70,000 vehicles built 2024, >100,000 in 2018; >90% exported. Plant had a planned non-production period Jun-Jul 2025. Electricity: rooftop solar phase 1 2 MWp (2022) + phase 2 12.6 MWp (R100m, from Q1 2024) = 14.6 MWp / 26,539 panels, sized to the plant's 12 MW peak demand and covering ~20% of annual MWh; MB group target >70% renewable energy in production by 2030 and CO2-neutral plants (via green power) - remaining ~80% of East London supply is the PPA opportunity.

commodity: Formerly Nissan Navara pickups (NP200 ended Mar 2024, Navara May 2026); from 2027 Chery/Jetour/Jaecoo SUVs
operations: Rosslyn assembly plant and nearby stamping plant sold by Nissan Motor Co to Chery SA (Chery Automobile, Wuhu, China); announced 23 Jan 2026, transfer completed 3 Jul 2026. Nissan South Africa (Pty) Ltd continues as importer/distributor only (Tekton, Patrol launches FY2026).
scale_note: Plant capacity 45,000/yr single shift, ~70,000 two-shift; output fell from 54,000 (2012) to ~25,000 and ~17,000 (2024); headcount 1,650 (Oct 2023) cut to ~800, of whom 692 transferred to Chery SA; Chery targets 40% local content and up to 3,000 direct+indirect jobs. No on-site solar, wheeled PPA or Scope 2 target published for Rosslyn under Nissan; Chery SA's energy plans not yet public - re-target this record at Chery SA.
status_flag: merged - now Chery SA (Rosslyn plant sold 3 Jul 2026; Nissan SA is sales-only)

commodity: Scania: truck and bus chassis assembly (CKD); MAN: truck assembly (Pinetown) and bus/coach bodies (Olifantsfontein)
operations: Two sister companies of Traton Group (Volkswagen AG). Scania South Africa (Pty) Ltd: new consolidated assembly plant at Aeroton, south of Johannesburg, opened Feb 2025 (replaced three sites). MAN Automotive (South Africa) (Pty) Ltd, wholly owned by MAN Truck & Bus SE: HQ Modderfontein, truck assembly plant Pinetown (KZN), bus/coach plant Olifantsfontein, parts depot Isando/Elandsfontein.
scale_note: Scania Aeroton: 3,200-3,600 units/yr capacity; 41,505 units assembled since 1995; no solar or PPA disclosed at opening. MAN Pinetown: described by MAN SA as 'the first carbon neutral plant in MAN' (2021) - basis (on-site solar vs offsets) not published on official pages; MAN SA MD publicly keen on solar (2025) and delivering first 10 electric buses in 2025. Employee counts not published for either. Traton/VW group target: net-carbon-neutral production sites.

commodity: Tyres — passenger, SUV, light truck and truck/bus radial (Dunlop, Sumitomo, Falken at Ladysmith; Bridgestone/Firestone at Brits)
operations: Three unrelated owners bundled. Sumitomo Rubber South Africa / Dunlop Tyres SA (Sumitomo Rubber Industries, Kobe): head office Durban, single plant at Ladysmith/uMnambithi, KZN. Bridgestone South Africa (Bridgestone Corp, Tokyo, via Bridgestone EMEA): single tyre plant at Brits, North West, plus retread sites (Gqeberha plant closed c.2020-21). Goodyear South Africa: Kariega (Uitenhage) plant CLOSED 15 Aug 2025 after 78 years; now sales, distribution and Hi-Q retail only.
scale_note: Sumitomo Ladysmith: nameplate 1,700 t/month; R2.1bn TBR plant (2018) plus R1.7bn passenger-tyre modernisation completed Aug 2026 (new mixer saves ~300 kWh, 60% waste cut); on-site solar 1 MW built with 6 MW in pipeline (2023); SRI target zero carbon 2050. Bridgestone Brits: 50 years old, ISO 50001 (2024), BSAF target 50% cut in manufacturing carbon footprint by 2027 via solar at Brits and alternative boiler fuel; Bridgestone group reports 100% renewable/low-carbon purchased electricity at 63 plants by end-2025 (Brits not itemised). Goodyear Kariega: 900+ jobs lost, no load. Employee counts not published on official pages for SRSA or BSAF.
status_flag: active (Sumitomo Ladysmith, Bridgestone Brits); closed - Goodyear Kariega plant shut 15 Aug 2025, Goodyear SA sales-only

commodity: Toyota Hilux (9th gen from Jul 2026), Fortuner, Corolla Cross, Hiace/Ses'fikile; Hino 300/500/700 trucks
operations: Prospecton plant, Durban (87 ha site; oldest Toyota plant outside Japan) incl. Hino SA truck plant on site; Toyota South Africa Motors (Pty) Ltd, wholly owned by Toyota Motor Corporation; head office Sandton; Atlas Road parts warehouse Boksburg
scale_note: Capacity 200,000+ vehicles/yr (Hilux 140,000/yr); ~8,500 employees at Prospecton per Jul 2026 press (TSA FY21 sustainability report: 6,388 full-time); R10.4bn 9th-gen Hilux programme (new logistics centre, chassis coating and welding plants to Jun 2027). Electricity: on-site solar 11.2 MWp by end-2023 (R239m), plus 3.8 MWp test-track and 0.9 MWp Hino in 2024, Hino roof 1.4 MWp; TSAM roadmap needs 34 MWp (R743m) to reach 100% renewable electricity by 2028 and carbon-neutral plant by 2035 - a ~15-20 MW gap that on-site roof space cannot close, i.e. wheeling candidate. FY21 production emissions 119 kt CO2, 860 kg CO2/vehicle. CEO cites electricity prices, water (new dam built) and rail as structural threats.

commodity: Volkswagen Polo (sole global source for Europe/Asia-Pacific, 38 markets), Polo Vivo; Tengo SUV from 2027; engines and components
operations: Plant Kariega (Uitenhage), Nelson Mandela Bay - vehicle plant, engine plant and component plant; Volkswagen Group Africa (Pty) Ltd, wholly owned by Volkswagen AG (Wolfsburg), also runs assembly in Kenya, Rwanda, Ghana; Group Parts warehouse Centurion
scale_note: Record 167,084 vehicles built 2024 (131,485 export Polos), record 17,009 in Jul 2026; three shifts; R4bn investment for third model (Tengo, SOP 2027). Electricity: on-site solar 5.2 MWp employee carport (R90m, 2024-25, 7,125-7,680 MWh/yr) plus 1.7 MWp final assembly roof, 1.0 MWp engine plant, 0.88 MWp component plant (Jun 2026), 0.2 MWp and 0.4 MWp (Centurion) = ~9.4 MWp; renewable share of production energy rose from 1.5% (2018) to 17.1% (2023) to 39.9% (2025) - the jump beyond on-site solar implies green-supply contracts, so a wheeled PPA sits inside an existing roadmap; goal Zero Impact Factory / carbon-neutral electricity by 2030. Headcount not published on official page found.
